item.title: Yakushiji: The Twin-Pagoda Temple of Nishinokyo — Guide
item.description: Yakushiji, in the Nishinokyo district west of central Nara, was founded in the late 7th century by an emperor praying for his consort’s recovery, and remains one of Japan’s most beautiful temple complexes. Its signature is symmetry: a pair of elegant three-story pagodas (that appear to have six roofs each) flank the Kondo hall, the East Pagoda an original 8th-century survivor and the West Pagoda a vivid modern reconstruction. Within the Kondo sits the Yakushi Triad, a magnificent bronze Medicine Buddha flanked by two bodhisattvas, counted among the supreme masterpieces of early Japanese Buddhist art.
